rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance: source of income (including Section 8 and public benefits) is a protected class in tenant selection
rules.requirement: The Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance bars discrimination in viewing or renting an apartment, in the terms and conditions of tenancy, and in advertising housing. Its protected categories include source of income, which covers Section 8 and public benefits. Landlords, sellers and rental agents may use any reasonable standard to select applicants, as long as they apply it equally and uniformly to all applicants. Selection may be based on the applicant's ability to pay the rent, ability to care for the apartment, and ability to respect the rights of others. The Cambridge Human Rights Commission enforces the ordinance. After a hearing, its remedies include a criminal complaint in District Court, civil fines of up to $300 per violation, a Superior Court action for injunctive relief, and damages. After a probable-cause finding, either party may remove a fair housing case to Superior Court or to the Attorney General's Office.
rules.key_value: Source of income (incl. Section 8 and public benefits) is protected; civil fines up to $300 per violation

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied 2-family dwelling (scope of the exemption as applied to source-of-income claims not stated)
coverage.summary: Applies to rental housing transactions in Cambridge. The official page notes an exemption for 2-family dwellings where the owner lives there.
coverage.owner_conditions: Exemption for 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there.

rules.exemptions: 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there (as described on the Commission page).
rules.effective_date_note: The documents give no adoption or effective date for ch. 14.04. They say only that the Human Rights Commission was established in 1984. The page presents the ordinance as currently enforced.
rules.quoted_span: Source of Income, includes Section 8 and public benefits
rules.review_note: The source is the Human Rights Commission's official page, not the ordinance text. It does not give the operative section number, so the citation is at chapter level. The page says nothing on criminal-history, credit or timing rules. It does not say whether the owner-occupied 2-family exemption reaches source-of-income claims. As context, the state bar on public-assistance and housing-subsidy discrimination (G.L. c. 151B, § 4(10)) has no owner-occupied two-family exemption. Voucher holders in an exempt Cambridge 2-family therefore remain protected under state law.
rules.source_notes: D029 says the protected-category list applies under both the Cambridge Human Rights Ordinance (ch. 2.76) and the Fair Housing Ordinance (ch. 14.04). Housing discrimination is handled under ch. 14.04, so ch. 2.76 is not used as an alias for this record. The cell candidate's alias 'Cambridge Human Rights Ordinance' is set aside for that reason.

rules.title: Cambridge Tenants Rights and Resources Ordinance: rights-and-resources Guide required at tenancy start and with any notice to quit or summary process
rules.requirement: Owners, landlords and management companies must give tenants the City's Tenants Rights and Resources Guide at the start of a tenancy. That means when the tenant first signs a lease, enters a tenancy agreement, or tenders the first month's rent. The Guide must be given again when legal steps to terminate a tenancy are taken, such as a Notice to Quit or Summary Process, at the same time as the notice or action. All tenants and lawful occupants, including tenants at will, must receive it. It is not required at lease renewals. A signed receipt is not required. The ordinance does not bar an eviction otherwise allowed by law. Violations may be fined $300 for each day's violation.
rules.key_value: Guide due at tenancy start and with any notice to quit or summary process; $300 fine per day of violation

unverifiable_exemptions: units in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is short-term assistance, treatment or therapy for alcohol, drug or other substance abuse
coverage.landlord_size_condition: Applies to all landlords, including an owner of a single rental unit in the building where the owner lives
coverage.summary: Applies to residential rental agreements in Cambridge, including single dwelling units and tenancies at will. Excludes units in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities, non-profit short-term substance-abuse treatment facilities, and Short Term Rental Units.
coverage.other_conditions: Excludes Short Term Rental Units under Cambridge Zoning Ordinance Art. 4, § 4.60, and units in hospitals, skilled nursing facilities, health facilities and non-profit short-term substance-abuse treatment facilities (see § 8.71.030 definitions).

rules.exemptions: Rental units in a hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; units in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is short-term assistance, treatment or therapy for alcohol, drug or other substance abuse; Short Term Rental Units under Cambridge Zoning Ordinance Art. 4, § 4.60.
rules.effective_date_note: The FAQ page does not state the ordinance's adoption or effective date. The page was posted 10/14/2020 and last modified 3/17/2025, so the ordinance was in force by the query date.
citation_aliases: Tenants Rights and Resources Notification Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The Ordinance also requires that a landlord provide the Guide to tenants when legal steps to terminate a tenancy are taken (ex. Notice to Quit or Summary Process).
rules.review_note: This is a notice requirement, not a list of allowed eviction causes. The documents show no Cambridge just-cause rule. The source is the City's official FAQ, not the ordinance text, and the operative section is not identified, so the citation is at chapter level. § 8.71.030 (definitions) and § 8.71.070 (penalty) are named in the FAQ. As context, the rule adds to the state form required with nonpayment notices to quit (G.L. c. 186, § 31). The Cambridge Guide is required with any termination step, not only for nonpayment, so both apply.
rules.source_notes: Both candidates rely on the same official City FAQ page (D031). The cell candidate's attribution to Cambridge is confirmed by the page title and text.
